audits.title: 1202 National Emergency Laparotomy Audit (NELA): Difficulties Achieving the Best Practice Tariff (BPT) Criteria
audits.standard: NELA Best Practice Tariff: 80% of NELA high-risk patients have consultant surgeon and consultant anaesthetist present during surgery and are admitted directly to critical care
audits.setting: Furness General Hospital, district general hospital, Barrow-in-Furness

cycle1.result: 57% of high-risk cases met BPT criteria; consultant surgeon present 100%; consultant anaesthetist 63% (37% SAS-grade anaesthetist); 87% admitted to critical care.

audits.other_findings: Of 43% not meeting BPT, 29 had no consultant anaesthetist, 6 not admitted to critical care and 8 both; survival 81% with SAS-grade anaesthetist versus 82% with consultant anaesthetist.
audits.citation: Chkir B, Patel P, Peris R, Lee G, Handa S. 1202 National Emergency Laparotomy Audit (NELA): Difficulties Achieving the Best Practice Tariff (BPT) Criteria. British Journal of Surgery. 2023;110(Supplement_7). doi:10.1093/bjs/znad258.374.

audits.title: Benchmarking against the National Emergency Laparotomy Audit recommendations.
audits.standard: National Emergency Laparotomy Audit (NELA) recommendations and outcomes (11.1% 30-day mortality)

cycle1.result: Total 30-day mortality 9.7% vs 11.1% reported by NELA.

audits.other_findings: Mortality at each P-POSSUM risk level was at the upper end of NELA; antibiotic timing, perioperative medical input and ICU admission did not differ between those who died and survived.
audits.citation: Ho YM, Cappello J, Kousary R, McGowan B, Wysocki AP. Benchmarking against the National Emergency Laparotomy Audit recommendations. ANZ J Surg. 2018;88(5):428-433. doi:10.1111/ans.14164. PMID: 28929609.

audits.title: Evaluation of the Collaborative Use of an Evidence-Based Care Bundle in Emergency Laparotomy.
audits.standard: 6-point evidence-based emergency laparotomy care bundle (lactate, sepsis review, time to theatre, goal-directed fluids, ICU admission, senior involvement)
audits.setting: 28 NHS hospitals in the Emergency Laparotomy Collaborative, NELA data
audits.intervention: Collaborative implementation of 6-point care bundle with change management and leadership coaching

cycle2.result: Unadjusted mortality 8.3% in year 2; risk-adjusted 4.5%; significant changes in 5 of 6 bundle metrics

audits.other_findings: Mean length of stay fell from 20.1 days in year 1 to 18.9 days in year 2.
audits.citation: Aggarwal G, Peden CJ, Mohammed MA, Pullyblank A, Williams B, Stephens T, et al.. Evaluation of the Collaborative Use of an Evidence-Based Care Bundle in Emergency Laparotomy. JAMA Surg. 2019;154(5):e190145. doi:10.1001/jamasurg.2019.0145. PMID: 30892581.

audits.title: Rural Emergency Laparotomy Audit.
audits.standard: Benchmarks of the National Emergency Laparotomy Audit and Perth Emergency Laparotomy Audit
audits.setting: Mount Gambier, Whyalla and Riverland hospitals; rural and regional South Australia; prospective multicentre audit

cycle1.result: 100% (51/51) had a consultant anaesthetist and surgeon present in theatre; no 30-day postoperative deaths; median P-POSSUM predicted mortality 3.5%.

audits.other_findings: Seven patients were transferred before surgery.
audits.citation: Watson MM, Maddern GJ, Mudalige VPK, Pradhan CP, Wichmann MW. Rural Emergency Laparotomy Audit. ANZ J Surg. 2019;89(6):666-671. doi:10.1111/ans.15167. PMID: 31083814.

audits.title: Closing the implementation gap: Process outcomes following a structured intraoperative bundle for emergency laparotomy.
audits.standard: EMLA intraoperative bundle (inspired by NELA): consultant anaesthesia and surgical care, goal-directed haemodynamic therapy for NELA score > 10, normothermia
audits.setting: Ng Teng Fong General Hospital, 700-bed tertiary hospital
audits.intervention: Structured intraoperative bundle introduced through iterative PDSA cycles.
audits.other_findings: 586 patients in total; GDHT adherence stayed high; consultant presence linked to a 42% relative reduction in medical complications; hypothermia persisted.
audits.citation: Baliga J, Iau P, Kavishwar P, Joseph J, Sebastian A. Closing the implementation gap: Process outcomes following a structured intraoperative bundle for emergency laparotomy. Indian J Anaesth. 2026;70(3):477-484. doi:10.4103/ija.ija_1716_25. PMID: 41907333.

audits.title: Two-year outcomes from the Australian and New Zealand Emergency Laparotomy Audit-Quality Improvement pilot study.
audits.standard: Eight evidence-based emergency laparotomy care standards (e.g. preoperative risk score, consultant presence, timely theatre and critical care access); green 80% or more

cycle1.result: Preoperative risk assessment overall 45%; timely theatre access 60%; 70% of those with predicted mortality over 10% admitted to critical care.

audits.intervention: Monthly QI run charts with traffic light feedback to participating hospitals.

cycle2.result: Preoperative risk assessment improved almost three-fold; in-hospital mortality 7.1% and length of stay both declined significantly.

audits.other_findings: Only 24 of 60 interested hospitals took part due to ethics approval difficulties.
audits.citation: ANZELA-QI Working Party, James Aitken R, Griffiths B, Van Acker J, O'Loughlin E, Fletcher D, et al.. Two-year outcomes from the Australian and New Zealand Emergency Laparotomy Audit-Quality Improvement pilot study. ANZ J Surg. 2021;91(12):2575-2582. doi:10.1111/ans.17037. PMID: 34184372.

audits.title: Perioperative emergency laparotomy pathway for patients undergoing emergency laparotomy: A propensity score matched study.
audits.standard: 8-item EMergency Laparotomy Audit (EMLA) perioperative care bundle
audits.setting: Ng Teng Fong General Hospital, single centre
audits.intervention: Interdisciplinary perioperative pathway with an 8-item bundle, involving specialist clinicians, administrators and a quality improvement team.

cycle2.result: Surgical complications 20.6%; hospitalisation cost SGD 30,948 (P=0.04); compliance with key interventions improved.

audits.other_findings: No difference in 30-day mortality; propensity score matching was used.
audits.citation: Lau JWL, Baliga J, Khan F, Teo YX, Yeo JMJ, Yeow VZ, et al.. Perioperative emergency laparotomy pathway for patients undergoing emergency laparotomy: A propensity score matched study. Ann Acad Med Singap. 2024;53(12):713-723. doi:10.47102/annals-acadmedsg.2024311. PMID: 39748170.

audits.title: Emergency Laparotomy in Regional New Zealand: Outcomes and Benchmarking Against NELA Standards.

cycle1.result: Preoperative CT 96% (95.2% consultant-reported); surgery within urgency timeframe 86.3%; consultant surgeon present 88.9%, consultant anaesthetist 100%; preoperative risk assessment documented in 4%.

audits.other_findings: Only 17.1% of patients aged 65 or over received geriatric assessment; 30-day mortality 10.3%; 42.9% admitted to critical care.
audits.citation: Yong LN, Leung E. Emergency Laparotomy in Regional New Zealand: Outcomes and Benchmarking Against NELA Standards. ANZ J Surg. 2026;96(7-8):1920-1926. doi:10.1111/ans.70783. PMID: 42265853.
